newsitem.title: JAPAN: TTNET SAYS TO START CHEAPEST CALL SERVICE IN JAPAN.
newsitem.headline: TTNET SAYS TO START CHEAPEST CALL SERVICE IN JAPAN.

text.p: The telecom affiliate of Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc said on Monday it would start city call and domestic long-distance call services at prices lower than Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT), DDI Corp, and Japan Telecom Co on January 7, 1998.
The low prices would be limited to residents of the greater Tokyo area.

TTNET, which is owned 33.4 percent by Tokyo Electric Power, will connect to NTT's local exchanges with its own optic fibre lines and offer city call services at nine yen per three minutes compared with NTT's ten yen per three minutes.
It will offer domestic long distance call services at 72 yen per three minutes, compared with 100 yen offered by DDI and Japan Telecom.
It will be first time there will be competition in the local call market, which is controlled by NTT.
TTNET said it aims to acquire 500,000 customers by the end of March 1998. Its breakeven point is two million customers, which it hopes to obtain by 1999.
Users will not need to pay initial joining fees or basic monthly fees and will be able to make calls by using adaptors which will be provided free of charge.
